rendering.persona_description: Nalani is a 53-year-old audiologist who has been married to her husband Mark for nineteen years. She runs a small practice out of a medical building and prides herself on being precise and thorough with patients, a trait that spills into the rest of her life. She has two adult children who are mostly out of the house now, and she spends a lot of her free time reading and gardening, though lately the gardening has fallen off.</br>
rendering.clinical_context: Nalani has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on doubts about whether she really loves her husband and whether their relationship is right, with intrusive comparisons to past partners and constant checking of her own feelings toward him. The doubts started subtly about four years ago and intensified after a close friend divorced, and she now spends significant parts of most days reviewing memories, testing her feelings, and asking Mark and friends for reassurance. She was diagnosed with OCD about a year ago but has not pursued treatment since, uncertain that therapy would address what feels to her like a real problem with her marriage rather than a psychological one.
rendering.behavioral_description: Nalani talks in a measured, articulate way, often building a case with examples as if she's presenting evidence, and she resists being told her doubts are 'just OCD' because to her they feel like real information about her marriage. She'll engage with suggestions and consider them, but pushes back when she feels dismissed, and she circles back to reassurance-seeking even while acknowledging on some level that it doesn't settle anything. She's skeptical that therapy would do more than relabel her doubts as 'just OCD,' rather than actually looking at whether something is wrong.
